source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Oral calcium alone because severe neuromuscular symptoms do not require rapid calcium replacement","B":"Intravenous calcium, commonly calcium gluconate, with appropriate cardiac and clinical monitoring","C":"Intravenous potassium chloride because potassium replacement directly corrects symptomatic hypocalcemia","D":"Loop diuretic therapy alone because increasing urinary calcium loss rapidly restores serum calcium"}}
source_row.rationale: Severe symptomatic hypocalcemia requires prompt intravenous calcium; calcium gluconate is commonly used. Cardiac monitoring is appropriate during IV treatment because rapid calcium administration can affect cardiac conduction.
source_row.source_detail: Treatment/Management: IV calcium for severe symptoms, prolonged QT, or acute hypocalcemia; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.stem: A client has tetany and other severe symptoms from confirmed hypocalcemia. Which treatment should the nurse anticipate for urgent correction?
